newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nemtsov sees 1.5-2.0 pct 98 Russia economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov sees 1.5-2.0 pct 98 Russia economic growth.

text.p: The Russian economy will grow next year but only at a modest 1.5-2.0 percent, rather less than other government predictions, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov forecast.
"We can attain economic growth next year," he told local businessmen in the region where he used to be a governor. "It will be a modest 1.5-2.0 percent economic growth."
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in May said 1998 growth would be at least two percent, a figure named a number of times by senior government officials.

Russian gross domestic product, the widest indicator of economic health, fell 0.4 percent in the year through May, although Chernomyrdin said the economy had grown one percent in the first six months of the year for the first time since economic reform began.
Nemtsov was Nizhny Novgorod campaigning on behalf of a candidate seeking to become governor, the office Nemtsov left to join the federal government.
